title: Employees Cost of Living Relief Act 1973

sections.shortTitle: Employees Cost of Living Relief Act 1973
sections.description:
Short title, extent and commencement

ACT I OF 1974
EMPLOYEES' COST OF LIVING
(RELIEF) ACT, 1973
ACT
I OF 1974
An Act to provide for payment of a cost of living allowance to employees
[Gazette
of Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part I, 7th January 1974]
The following Act
of Parliament received the assent of the President on the 31st December 1973,
and is hereby published for general information :‑
1. Short
title, extent and commencement.‑(1) This Act may be called the
Employees' Cost of Living (Relief) Act, 1973.
(2) It shall
come into force at once. (3) It extends to the whole of Pakistan.

sections.shortTitle: Employees Cost of Living Relief Act 1973

Definitions

ACT I OF 1974
EMPLOYEES' COST OF LIVING
(RELIEF) ACT, 1973
ACT
I OF 1974
An Act to provide for payment of a cost of living allowance to employees
[Gazette
of Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part I, 7th January 1974]
The following Act
of Parliament received the assent of the President on the 31st December 1973,
and is hereby published for general information :‑
2.
Definitions.‑(I) In this Act, unless there is anything repugnant in
the subject or context,‑
(a) "cost
of living allowance" means the amount payable under the provisions of this
Act;
(b)
"employee" means any person employed, whether directly or through any
other person, for wages, to do any skilled or unskilled, intellectual,
technical, clerical, manual or other work in, or is connection with the affairs
of, an undertaking, under any contract of service or apprenticeship, whether
written or oral, express or implied, and includes such a person when laid off.
but does not include a person employed on wages equal to, or exceeding, seven
hundred and thirty‑five rupees per month, or a person for whom a
provision has been, or may be, made by the Federal Government or a Provincial
Government for grant of an allowance intended to provide relief due to a rise
fn the cost of living;
(c)
"employer", in relation to an undertaking, means any person who
employs, either directly or through any other person, whether on behalf of
himself or any other person, any employee, and Includes‑
(i) a
body of persons, whether incorporated or not;
(ii) a
person who has ultimate control over the affairs of an undertaking, Including
the owner of the undertaking, or where the affairs of any under. taking are
entrusted to any other person (whether called a managing agent, director, manager,
agent, superintendent, secretary, representative of the owner or by any other
name), such other person, or in any other case, any person responsible to the
owner for supervision and control of an employee or for payment of his wages;
and
(iii) an heir,
successor, administrator or assign, as the case may be, of ouch person or
association of persons;
(d)
"undertaking" means‑
(i) an
establishment to which the West Pakistan Shops and Establishments Ordinance,
1969 (W. P. Ordinance No. VIII of 1969), for the time being applies, and,
notwithstanding anything contained in section 5 thereof, includes clubs,
hostels and messes not maintained for profit or gain and establishments for the
treatment or care of the sick, infirm, and destitute or mentally unfit persons;
(ii) a
construction industry to which the West Pakistan Industrial and Commercial
Employment (Standing Orders) Ordinance, 1968 (W. P. Ordi nance No. VI of 1968)
for the time being applies;
(iii) a
factory as defined in the Factories Act, 1934 (XXV of 1934);
(iv) a
mine as defined in the Mines Act, 1923 (IV of 1923);
(v) a road
transport service as defined In the Road Transport Workers Ordinance, 1961
(XXVIII of 1961);
(vi) a newspaper
establishment as defined in the Newspaper Employees,, (Conditions of Service)
Act, 1973 (LVIII of 1973); and
includes any class of
establishments which the Federal Government may, by notification In the
official Gazette, declare to be undertakings for the purposes of this Act;
(e)
"wages" means remuneration for services, other than cost of living
allowance, payable in cash to an employee without taking account of' deductions
for any purpose, under a contract of service or apprenticeship, written, oral,
express or implied, and includes any dearness allowance or other addition in
respect of the cost of living payable or paid for there period preceding the
first day of August 1973, and any payment by the employer to an employee in
respect of any period of authorised leave, butt does not include‑
(i) any
payment for overtime, or
(ii) any sum
paid to an employee to defray special expenses entailed by the nature of his
employment ; or
(iii) any
gratuity payable on discharge; or
(iv) any sum
paid as bonus, house rent, conveyance al

5. Time for
payment of cost of living allowance.‑The cost of living allowance
shall be paid along with wages in accordance with any custom,. usage, practice
or law applicable to the undertaking:
Provided that
where an employee employed in an establishment has not. been paid the cost of
living allowance for any period commencing on or after the first day of August
1973, but preceding the commencement of this Act, the employer shall pay it to
him within thirty days of such com mencement.

6. Claims for
recovery, or delay In payment, of cost of living allowance---. Where
contrary to the provisions of this Act, the cost of living allowance of and
employee has been withheld or delayed, such worker himself or through and other
person authorised by him in this behalf may apply‑
(a) in the case
of an establishment to which tire West Pakistan Shops end Establishments
Ordinance, 1969 (W. P. Ordinance No. VIII of 1969), for the time being applies,
to the authority appointed under subsection (1) of section 12 thereof having jurisdiction and the
provisions of the said section and
sections 11, 13, 21, 23, 30 and 32 of that Ordinance shall, so far as may be
and with the necessary modifications, apply for the purposes of recovery of the
cost of living allowance; and
(b) in any
other ease, to the authority appointed tinder subsection (1) o; section 15 of
the Payment of Wages Act, 1936 (IV of 1936), having { i and the provisions of
the said section and sections 6, 16, 17, 18, 19, 22, 23 and 26 of the said Act
shall, so far as may be and with the necessary modifications, apply for the
purposes of recovery of the cost of living allowance.

sections.shortTitle: Employees Cost of Living Relief Act 1973
sections.description:
Cost of living allowance not to form part of Wages

ACT I OF 1974
EMPLOYEES' COST OF LIVING
(RELIEF) ACT, 1973
ACT
I OF 1974
An Act to provide for payment of a cost of living allowance to employees
[Gazette
of Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part I, 7th January 1974]
The following Act
of Parliament received the assent of the President on the 31st December 1973,
and is hereby published for general information :‑
7. Cost of
living allowance not to form part of wages.‑Notwithstanding anything
contained in this Act or any other law for the time being in force, the cost of
living allowance shall not form part of wages of a worker for the purposes of
any other law, including the purposes of contribution to provident fund.
gratuity. bonus, social security scheme and calculating wages for over‑time
work.

sections.shortTitle: Employees Cost of Living Relief Act 1973
sections.description:
Saving of certain rights and privileges

ACT I OF 1974
EMPLOYEES' COST OF LIVING
(RELIEF) ACT, 1973
ACT
I OF 1974
An Act to provide for payment of a cost of living allowance to employees
[Gazette
of Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part I, 7th January 1974]
The following Act
of Parliament received the assent of the President on the 31st December 1973,
and is hereby published for general information :‑
8. Saving of
certain rights and privileges.‑Nothing in this Act shall affect any
right or privilege to which an employee was entitled immediately before the
commencement of the Employees' Cost of Living (Relief) Ordinance, 1973 (XXII of
1973), under any law for the time being in force or under any award, agreement,
settlement, contract, custom or usage in force immediately before such
commencements;
Provided that,
if, on or after the first day of August 1973, but preceding the commencement of
the said Ordinance, any employer has paid, or agreed to pay, whether by way of
settlement or otherwise, to any employee, in respect o‑f any period, any
sum of money, whether as an allowance not forming part of his wages or as
increase in wages or otherwise, which is intended to provide relief due to a
rise in the coat of living, such employer shall not be required to pay to such
employee any amount in excess of the difference, if any, between the amount so
paid by him and the cost of living allowance payable to such employee.

9. Penalty.‑Any
employer who contravenes any provision of this Act shall be punishable with
simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or wish fine
which may extend to two thousand rupees, or with both.

Cost of living allowance in addition to that admissible under section 3

EMPLOYEES' COST OF LIVING (RELIEF) ACT, 1973
EMPLOYEES' COST OF LIVING
(RELIEF) ACT, 1973
ACT
I OF 1974
An Act to provide for payment of a cost of living allowance to employees
[Gazette
of Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part I, 7th January 1974]
The following
Act of Parliament received the assent of the President on the 31st December
1973, and is hereby published for general information :‑
3A ‑‑ Cost of living allowance in addition to that
admissible under section 3.( Subs. new s. 3A by
Employees Cost of living (Relief) (Amendment) Act, 1992 (Act XXVII of 1992),
Gaz. of Pak. Extra., Pt. I. December 17, 1992, p. 651-652, replacing the old s.
3A by Ord. XIX of 1991, s. 2. Only two changes made: 1) new s. 3S came force
from 1st instead of 30th of December, 1990, and 2) words
not exceeding twenty-five percent of his wages were omitted and subs. by and
in such area or areas. )
In addition to the cost of living
allowance admissible under section 3, if any, every employee shall, in respect
of his employment on or after the first day of December, 1990; whether on time‑work
of piece‑work basis, be paid by his employer, a cost of living allowance
at such rate and in such area, or areas as the Federal Government pray, by
notification in the official Gazette specify].
COMMENTARY
To the minimum wage, add the following
COLAs, Federal as well as provincial (not given here), to get the current
minimum wage anywhere in tine country):
(i) Rs. 100/-COLA (Aug.
1993.): With effect from September, 1, 1993, every employee is to be paid a
cost of living a allowance (i) equal to Rs. 100 p.m. if his wages do not exceed
Rs. 4065 p.m. or (ii) at such rate as, together with his wages, makes a total
of Rs. 4165 p.m., if his wages are more than Rs. 4065 p.m.
(ii) Rs. 50/-COLA (March
1994): From April 1, 1994, all employees regardless of wages drawn, are to
be paid cost of living allowance of Rs. 50 P.m.
(iii) Rs. 300/‑ COLA
(March 1997): From March 1, 1997, every employee whose terms and conditions
of employment are negotiable through CBA under IRO shall be paid an ad hoc
relief of Rs. 300/-p.m., if his wages do not exceed Rs. 4065/‑ p.m.
(iv) Rs. 300/‑ COLA
(June 1998): The above March 1997 Notification is suppressed and replaced
with June 1998 Notification regularizing tile old rd hoc relief of Rs. 300/-pm.
Hence, it is not a new COLA to be given in addition to March 1997 COLA,
however, its terms and conditions were changed. Under June 1998 Notification,
every employee shall be paid a cost of living allowance of Rs. 300/‑ p.m.
omitting all references to wage limits and other restrictions.
